decisions.rationale: Whimsicott + Mega Metagross handles both predicted leads: Prankster Tailwind or Encore lets Metagross outspeed and KO Garchomp with Ice Punch (4x) or pressure Floette with Meteor Mash (2x). decisions.notebook: Game 2, series 1-0. Opponent's likely leads: Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin, EQ) + Rotom-Wash (Sitrus, Hydro Pump) or Talonflame (Sharp Beak, Gale Wings) + Floette-Mega (Floettite, Light of Ruin). Garchomp EQs aggressively; Rotom-Wash spams Hydro Pump. Floette-Mega stalls with Protect. Archaludon Flash Cannon + Expert Belt 2HKOes Floette-Mega. Quaquaval Moxie snowballs after KO. Floette-Mega Protect success drops after turn 7+. Remaining threats: Dragapult (Focus Sash, Infiltrator, Phantom Force, Will-O-Wisp) and Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant, Rage Fist, Close Combat). Plan: Whimsicott Prankster Tailwind/Encore enables Mega Metagross to outspeed and KO. Archaludon Stalwart Draco Meteor bypasses Protect. Quaquaval Liquidation for high damage, keep healthy due to -1 Def/-1 SpD vulnerability. Note: Quaquaval Close Combat does 0 to Annihilape (Ghost immunity); use Liquidation or Ice Spinner instead.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp+Rotom-Wash lead exploits Levitate for safe EQ while Hydro Pump threatens Metagross. Against Whimsicott+Metagross: Garchomp Protects turn 1 as Rotom pressures Meta; Rock Slide+VoltSwitch break Whimsicott sash turn 2. Against Grimmsnarl screens: EQ hits through. Floette-Mega (Fairy Aura) and Annihilape (RageFist 2x Meta, CloseCombat 2x Arch) provide strong endgame coverage. decisions.notebook: Game 1 Talonflame ineffective vs Whimsicott teams — bench if Whimsicott expected. Dragapult Dragon Darts completely blocked by Fairy (Whimsicott); not a Whimsicott answer. Floette-Mega Fairy Aura boosts all Fairy moves on field. Annihilape Rage Fist super-effective (2x) on Metagross; Close Combat super-effective (2x) on Archaludon. Opponent likely brings Whimsicott+Metagross core each game. Future: consider double-targeting Whimsicott to break Focus Sash in one turn; Garchomp Rock Slide (spread) + partner single-target works. Grimmsnarl screens extend opponent bulk — breakers needed.

decisions.rationale: Base Metagross (92) is outsped by Garchomp (117-169) and takes 2x from Life Orb Earthquake. Tailwind + Protect guarantees Metagross survives turn 1 and sets up Tailwind. Next turn, Mega Metagross with Tailwind (230-324 effective speed) outspeeds Garchomp and KO's with 4x super-effective Ice Punch, establishing board control.

Rock Slide avoids Encore risk (Garchomp hasn't moved yet when Prankster Encore fires, so Encore fails). Combined with Hydro Pump threatens KO on Whimsicott before it acts again; even if Tailwind goes up, removing Whimsicott denies future Encores and second Tailwind. Rock Slide also chips Metagross. If they double Garchomp and Whimsicott outspeeds, Garchomp may fall but gets Rock Slide off.

decisions.rationale: Encore locks Rotom-Wash into Hydro Pump (0.5x vs Whimsicott), removing immediate threat to 34% Whimsicott. reflections.summary: Lost due to a flawed team preview plan. Metagross-Mega was too slow and fainted to Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump while targeting a Protecting Floette. Whimsicott's Tailwind failed, and it fainted to Volt Switch. Archaludon's Draco Meteor dropped its SpA, and it couldn't break through Garchomp's Protect or Annihilape's Close Combat (which was super effective). Quaquaval wasted a turn attacking Annihilape's Protect and was KO'd by Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch. The opponent's Annihilape + Rotom-Wash core ove
reflections.adjustment: Drop Metagross-Mega from the preview against this team; it's too slow and weak to Rotom-Wash. Bring a faster attacker that can pressure Annihilape and Rotom-Wash before they act, and consider a Grass-type or strong Electric move to handle Rotom-Wash. Avoid relying on Whimsicott's Tailwind as the sole speed control, as it can fail.
reflections.notebook: Opponent leads Garchomp (LO, Rough Skin) + Rotom-Wash (Sitrus Berry). Garchomp uses Protect frequently to block double targets. Annihilape (Leftovers, Defiant) uses Close Combat (super effective vs Archaludon) and Protect; Defiant boosts Attack when stats drop. Rotom-Wash uses Hydro Pump, Volt Switch, Will-O-Wisp; Sitrus Berry provides healing. Floette-Eternal stalls with Protect and hits hard with Light of Ruin. Talonflame (Gale Wings, Sharp Beak) and Dragapult (Focus Sash, Infiltrator) are back threats. Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind can fail and be lost. Archaludon's Draco Meteor drops SpA by 2, reducing its breaking power over time. Opponent's strategy: use Protect to block attacks, wear down with Rotom-Wash + Annihilape core.

reflections.summary: We won because we successfully stalled out the opponent's Tailwind turns with Protect and pivots, eliminating their speed control (Whimsicott) and special wallbreaker (Archaludon) early. Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump KO on Metagross and Volt Switch pivoting were pivotal, while Annihilape's Close Combats cleaned up. The opponent's misplay of a failed Tailwind on turn 4 and their inability to break our defensive core allowed us to preserve all four Pokémon and win without losses.
reflections.adjustment: For Game 3, expect the opponent to bring Grimmsnarl and Stunfisk to set screens and spread paralysis. Lead with Floette-Eternal and Rotom-Wash to pressure Grimmsnarl with Fairy damage and threaten burns, while keeping Annihilape in the back to deter Parting Shot with Defiant and clean up late-game. Preserve Garchomp to handle Stunfisk's Ground typing and block Volt Switch.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's full roster: Metagross-Mega (Adamant, Ice Punch/Meteor Mash/EQ/Protect), Whimsicott (Timid, Focus Sash, Encore/Tailwind/Moonblast/Protect), Quaquaval (Adamant, Life Orb, Moxie, Liquidation/Close Combat/Ice Spinner/Protect), Archaludon (Modest, Expert Belt, Stalwart, Flash Cannon/Draco Meteor/Thunderbolt/Protect), Stunfisk-Galar (Impish, Leftovers, Mimicry, EQ/Crunch/Thunder Wave/Protect), Grimmsnarl (Careful, Light Clay, Prankster, Reflect/Light Screen/Spirit Break/Parting Shot). In Game 2 they led Metagross + Whimsicott with Quaquaval + Archaludon back, prioritizing Tailwind and Encore disruption. Their physical attackers are vulnerable to burns and Rough Skin. Stunfisk and Grimmsnarl remain unused; expect them in Game 3 to set screens and spread paralysis. Floette-Eternal's Light of Ruin is key for breaking screens. Annihilape's Defiant deters Parting Shot. Plan: lead with Floette + Rotom to pressure Grimmsnarl, pivot with Volt Switch/U-turn, and stall Tailwind with Protect. Use Garchomp to threaten Stunfisk and block Volt Switch. Preserve Annihilape for late-game cleanup.
